items.label: Activities overview
items.details: Shows all windows and workspaces; start typing right away to search for apps, files and settings.

items.label: Show all apps
items.details: Opens the app grid.

items.label: Switch apps
items.details: Hold Alt and keep pressing Tab to cycle through open apps; Shift goes backwards. Super+Tab does the same.

items.label: Switch windows of the app
items.details: Cycles between windows of the current app. ` is the key above Tab, whatever your layout prints on it.

items.label: Tile left / right
items.details: Fills the left or right half of the screen with the window; press again to restore it.

items.label: Maximize / restore
items.details: Maximizes the window, or restores its previous size.

items.label: Hide window
items.details: Minimizes the focused window.

items.label: Close window
items.details: Closes the focused window.

items.label: Previous / next workspace
items.details: Switches workspace. Super+Alt+← / → and Ctrl+Alt+← / → do the same.

items.label: Move window to workspace
items.details: Takes the focused window along to the previous or next workspace.

items.label: Move window to monitor
items.details: Sends the focused window to the monitor in that direction.

items.label: Notifications and calendar
items.details: Opens the notification list with the calendar. Super+M does the same.

items.label: Quick settings
items.details: Opens the system menu with Wi-Fi, sound, power and the light/dark switch.

items.label: Switch keyboard layout
items.details: Cycles through the configured input sources.

items.label: Lock the screen
items.details: Locks the session immediately.

items.label: Run a command
items.details: Opens a one-line prompt to run a command without a terminal.

items.label: Screenshot tool
items.details: Opens the screenshot tool: pick an area, a window or the whole screen, or switch to recording. Shots land in Pictures/Screenshots and on the clipboard.

items.label: Whole screen right away
items.details: Takes a screenshot of the whole screen without asking.

items.label: Focused window right away
items.details: Takes a screenshot of the focused window without asking.

items.label: Record the screen
items.details: Opens the tool in recording mode; the same keys stop the recording. Videos land in Videos/Screencasts.

items.label: Undo / redo
items.details: Works in nearly every text field and editor.

items.label: Word back / forward
items.details: Moves the cursor a word at a time; add Shift to select while moving.

items.label: Delete the previous word
items.details: Deletes back to the start of the word. Ctrl+Delete deletes forwards.

items.label: Select to line start / end
items.details: Selects from the cursor to the start or end of the line.

items.label: Emoji picker
items.details: Opens the emoji chooser in GTK apps. Ctrl+; works too.

items.label: Type a Unicode character
items.details: Then type the hex code and press Space or Enter: Ctrl+Shift+U 2014 gives an em dash.

items.label: Search command history
items.details: Type part of an old command; Ctrl+R again goes further back, Enter runs it, an arrow key puts it on the line to edit.

items.label: Start / end of line
items.details: Moves the cursor to the beginning or end of the line.

items.label: Word back / forward
items.details: Moves the cursor a word at a time.

items.label: Delete the previous word
items.details: Deletes the word left of the cursor; Ctrl+Y pastes it back.

items.label: Delete to end of line
items.details: Deletes from the cursor to the end of the line; Ctrl+Y pastes it back.

items.label: Paste what was just deleted
items.details: Pastes the text last deleted with Ctrl+W, Ctrl+K or Ctrl+U.

items.label: Previous command's last argument
items.details: Inserts the last argument of the previous command; press again to go further back. Example: mkdir foo, then cd Alt+.

items.label: Undo
items.details: Undoes the last edit to the command line.

items.label: Clear the screen
items.details: Clears the terminal and keeps the line being typed.

items.label: Cancel / end input
items.details: Ctrl+C stops the running command or drops the line. Ctrl+D on an empty line ends input, which closes the shell.

items.label: Pause the running command
items.details: Suspends it and returns to the prompt; fg brings it back, bg lets it continue in the background.
